papers.title: From saccharides to methane: substrate-driven microbial diversity and methanogenesis in anaerobic digestion revealed by 390 MAGs.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) is a key technology for organic waste treatment and renewable energy production, yet its microbial processes remain poorly understood. This study employed genome-centric metagenomics to investigate synthetic AD systems fed with five substrates: starch, glucose, butyrate, propionate-valerate, and acetate. A total of 390 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) were reconstructed, 64.36% of which represent potentially novel species. Substrate-driven selection shaped distinct functional consortia, with Bifidobacterium enriched in starch hydrolysis and Syntrophomon
papers.summary: This study used genome-centric metagenomics to reconstruct 390 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from synthetic anaerobic digestion systems fed with five different substrates (starch, glucose, butyrate, propionate-valerate, and acetate). Nearly two-thirds of the MAGs represent potentially novel species, and the authors show that substrate type drives selection of distinct functional microbial consortia, with specific taxa enriched for particular degradation steps (e.g., Bifidobacterium in starch hydrolysis). The work provides a large genome resource and links substrate chemistry to community structure and methanogenesis pathways.

papers.title: Taxonova: Deep learning enables fast and confidence-aware microbiome species-level amplicon classification.
papers.abstract: Accurate species-level taxonomic classification of microbial amplicon sequences remains challenging due to the difficulty of resolving subtle variations within conserved ribosomal regions. Traditional similarity-based methods struggle with short amplicons and sequences with poor database representation. No existing method performs robustly across the full spectrum of amplicon lengths, limiting applicability across diverse sequencing platforms and variable-region targets. We present Taxonova, a deep learning framework for both short- and long-read ribosomal amplicons. Evaluated across physical
papers.summary: Taxonova is a deep learning framework that classifies microbial amplicon sequences at the species level for both short- and long-read sequencing platforms. It addresses the limitations of similarity-based methods by learning subtle variation patterns in conserved ribosomal regions and providing confidence-aware predictions, aiming for robust performance across diverse amplicon lengths and variable-region targets.

papers.title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures.
papers.abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited in
papers.summary: This study longitudinally profiles the upper respiratory virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using optimized viral enrichment and metagenomic sequencing. The authors find that viral communities show phage-driven adaptation and evolutionary signatures shared with viruses from other hosts, suggesting cross-host transmission or common ancestry at the human-animal interface.

papers.title: Nutrient control enables metabolic reconstruction of Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG and analysis of secretions.
papers.abstract: Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) is an important gut commensal bacterial strain that has been extensively studied in both industrial and health settings. Despite its long history of study, a high-quality genome-scale metabolic network model (GEM) for LGG has yet to be reconstructed. Only automatically generated draft models have been published, which have notoriously limited functional accuracy. Furthermore, comprehensive nutrient requirements have not been established for well-controlled in vitro studies. Here, we present the first curated GEM for LGG using a new approach for reconstruct
papers.summary: The authors present the first manually curated genome-scale metabolic model for the probiotic gut bacterium Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus GG, built using a new nutrient-controlled reconstruction approach. They also establish comprehensive nutrient requirements for well-controlled in vitro growth studies and analyze the bacterium's secretions. This provides a more accurate metabolic framework for studying LGG physiology and its interactions with the gut environment.

papers.title: CNTN4: A Possible Candidate Gene for Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota plays a significant role in autism spectrum disorders (ASD) and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), though findings vary substantially across studies. Using gut microbiome data from a genome-wide association study of 5,959 participants and summary statistics from 46,351 ASD and 55,374 ADHD cases, we conducted bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses with inverse variance weighting as the primary method. Reverse MR analysis assessed potential reverse causality. We annotated single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) with SNP-nexus to identify associated ge
papers.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
papers.summary: This study used bidirectional Mendelian randomization to test causal relationships between gut microbiome features and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and ADHD, drawing on large GWAS datasets. The authors identify CNTN4 as a possible candidate gene linking the microbiota-gut-brain axis to both conditions. The work suggests shared genetic pathways may underlie microbiome-mediated risk for these neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Role of Gut Microbiota-derived Metabolites in the Pathogenesis and Progression of Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely linked with significant comorbidities and mortality. Evidence suggests that gut microbiota-derived metabolites play a vital role in the initiation and progression of MASLD. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the role of these metabolites in the pathogenesis and progression of MASLD, including steatosis, steatohepatitis, fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
papers.journal: Journal of gastrointestinal and liver diseases : JGLD
papers.summary: This systematic review examines how metabolites produced by gut bacteria contribute to the development and progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), from simple fat accumulation through inflammation, fibrosis, and liver cancer. It synthesizes existing evidence linking microbial metabolic products to each stage of disease, highlighting the gut-liver axis as a driver of MASLD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Modeling association networks from metagenome time series - a proof-of-concept from two contrasting estuaries.
papers.abstract: Understanding microbial responses to environmental gradients is important for ecosystem assessment in estuarine environments. Here, we integrated time-series samples and shotgun metagenomics with association network inference, to examine patterns of taxonomic and functional co-variation. We collected and sequenced eDNA from two sediment time series from neighbouring but environmentally contrasting Basque estuaries, and compared the resulting taxonomic and functional association networks, based on Metagenome Assembled Genomes (MAGs) and KEGG Orthologous Groups (KOs), respectively. Networks infe
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study combined time-series eDNA sampling with shotgun metagenomics and association network inference to compare microbial co-variation patterns in two neighboring but environmentally contrasting Basque estuaries. Taxonomic networks were built from Metagenome Assembled Genomes (MAGs) and functional networks from KEGG Orthologous Groups (KOs), allowing comparison of how community structure and function co-vary across environmental gradients. The work demonstrates a framework for using network inference on metagenomic time series to assess estuarine ecosystem dynamics.

papers.title: Bacterial community profiles of soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve, Philippines.
papers.abstract: The Mount Makiling Forest Reserve harbors diverse microorganisms with potential biotechnological applications, yet bacterial taxonomic profiling across its watersheds remains limited. Amplicon metagenome sequencing targeting the 16S rRNA gene revealed Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota as dominant phyla, with Actinobacteriota, Verrucomicrobiota, Chloroflexi, Myxococcota, Methylomirabilota, Bacteroidota, Nitrospirota, and Planctomycetota present at varying abundances.
papers.summary: This study used 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to profile bacterial communities in soils from the Mount Makiling Forest Reserve in the Philippines. Proteobacteria and Acidobacteriota were the dominant phyla, with ten additional phyla present at varying abundances across watersheds. The work provides a baseline taxonomic survey of an understudied tropical forest soil microbiome.

papers.title: Causal effects between gut microbiology and hyperlipidemia: A 2-sample Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Recent studies have confirmed the connection between gut microbiota (GM) and hyperlipidemia. This study used the Mendelian randomization (MR) technique to explore the association between GM and hyperlipidemia. MR was used to examine data derived from a genome-wide association study that combined data from 211 intestinal microbiota and hyperlipidemia. Five statistical tools were used for statistical analyses, including the MR-Egger method, the weighted median method, the inverse variance weighted method, the simple model, and the weighted mode. Inverse variance weighted is the main type among t
papers.summary: This study applied two-sample Mendelian randomization to test whether gut microbiota composition causally affects hyperlipidemia risk, using GWAS summary data for 211 microbial taxa and hyperlipidemia. Multiple MR methods (IVW as primary, plus MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, and simple mode) were used to estimate causal effects. The work provides genetic-evidence-based support for links between specific gut microbes and hyperlipidemia, though the abstract does not report which taxa were significant.

papers.title: A cow individual milk fat percentage prediction method based on low-rank multimodal fusion of time-series, numerical, and textual data.
papers.abstract: Milk fat percentage (MFP) precise prediction is paramount for precision dairy farming and early warning of health issues. However, existing prediction methods primarily rely on single lactation time-series data or statistical models, which often fail to effectively fuse multi-source heterogeneous information and frequently overlook the impact of individual variability. To address current limitations, long short-term memory(LSTM), Stacking ensemble learning,bidirectional encoder representations from transformers(BERT) and low-rank multimodal fusion(LMF) were employed to explore a hierarchical m
papers.summary: This study develops a multimodal machine learning framework that predicts individual cow milk fat percentage by fusing three heterogeneous data sources: lactation time-series data (via LSTM), numerical features (via Stacking ensemble learning), and textual records (via BERT), combined through low-rank multimodal fusion. The approach aims to capture individual variability and multi-source information that single-source or statistical models overlook, supporting precision dairy farming and early health warning.

papers.title: From Microbiome Profiling to Clinical Translation: Designing microbiome studies for clinical actionability.
papers.abstract: Microbiome research has identified many highly valuable associations between microbial communities and factors such as diet, antibiotics use, lifestyle, inflammation, infection and chronic disease. However, many findings remain difficult to translate into clinical practice because they are only association-based and vulnerable to confounding. Many studies also often lack reproducibility. Comparisons between "dysbiotic" and "healthy" microbiome states can be misleading because microbiome profiles are shaped by factors such as diet, medication, geography, host genetics, demographics, disease sev
papers.summary: This perspective argues that most microbiome-disease associations remain difficult to translate into clinical practice because they are correlational, vulnerable to confounding, and often not reproducible. The authors propose principles for designing microbiome studies with clinical actionability in mind, cautioning that simple 'dysbiotic vs. healthy' comparisons are misleading given how diet, medication, geography, host genetics, and demographics shape microbiome profiles.

papers.title: Hospital Drain Microbiomes as Distinct Microbial Signatures Within Urban Wastewater Networks in the Han River Watershed.
papers.abstract: Background: Hospital drainage systems represent an important interface between healthcare facilities and urban wastewater networks and may contribute distinct microbial inputs to downstream aquatic environments. This issue is particularly relevant in Seoul, Republic of Korea, where urban wastewater discharges into receiving waters within the Han River watershed. Methods: In this study, we characterized hospital drain microbiomes to evaluate their microbial and environmental signatures, using residential drains as a non-clinical comparison. Results: Hospital drains exhibited a distinct taxonomi
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiomes of hospital drains to residential drains within Seoul's urban wastewater network, finding that hospital drains harbor distinct taxonomic signatures. These differences suggest healthcare facilities contribute unique microbial inputs to downstream waters in the Han River watershed, with potential implications for environmental and public health monitoring.

papers.title: Machine Learning in Mammals' Health: Integrating Multi-Omics Data for Precision Nutrition and Sustainable Production.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrition in modern mammalian production aims to transition from static feeding regimens toward dynamic and customized strategies by unraveling complex interactions among genetics, environment, the gut microbiome, and host physiology. Machine learning provides a powerful analytical framework to navigate high-dimensional multi-omics datasets. However, existing applications frequently lack systematic criteria for algorithm selection and remain largely confined to observational statistical associations without progressing toward causal verification. This perspective delineates a coheren
papers.summary: This perspective argues that precision nutrition in mammalian production should move beyond static feeding regimens by integrating multi-omics data (genetics, microbiome, physiology) through machine learning. The authors highlight that current ML applications often lack systematic criteria for algorithm selection and remain limited to observational associations rather than causal verification, and they outline a coherent framework for advancing toward causal, customized feeding strategies.

papers.title: Shenqi Granules Ameliorate Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury by Regulating Glucocerebrosidase and Uridine Metabolism in Microglia.
papers.abstract: Objective: Shenqi Granules is a traditional Chinese medicine formula derived from the classic prescription Shenqi Formula (SQF), composed of Astragali Radix (Huangqi) and Codonopsis Radix (Dangshen). SQF shows neuroprotection in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Methods: The rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) was established using the suture method to evaluate the neuroprotective effect of SQF. Blood-absorbed components were identified via UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, and potential targets and pathways were predicted through netw
papers.summary: This study shows that Shenqi Granules, a traditional Chinese medicine formula, protect against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats by modulating glucocerebrosidase activity and uridine metabolism in microglia. The authors combined a rat MCAO model with blood-absorbed component identification and network pharmacology to link the formula's constituents to these metabolic targets. The work suggests a microglial metabolic mechanism for the formula's neuroprotective effects.

papers.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring for Metabolic Phenotyping and Precision Nutrition: Current Evidence, Clinical Applications and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has evolved beyond conventional diabetes management into an enabling technology for metabolic phenotyping and precision nutrition by providing continuous, real-world assessment of individual glycemic responses to dietary and lifestyle exposures. This narrative review examines the principles and clinical utility of CGM and its emerging applications in metabolic monitoring and personalized nutrition, with particular emphasis on postprandial glycemic variability, computational prediction, dietary feedback, and behavioral interventions. A literature search was c
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has expanded beyond diabetes care into metabolic phenotyping and precision nutrition, focusing on postprandial glycemic variability, computational prediction of glucose responses, and dietary/behavioral feedback interventions. It summarizes current evidence and clinical applications while outlining future directions for using CGM to personalize nutrition.

papers.title: Next-Generation Functional Nanoplatforms: Engineering Plant-Derived Extracellular Vesicles for Targeted Bioactive Delivery and Health Applications.
papers.abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) are being recognized as a capable novel class of natural nanocarriers that have important uses in delivering bioactives and facilitating innovations in functional foods and precision health technologies. PDEVs are lipid-bilayer-enclosed vesicular structures that commonly occur at the nanoscale, although their reported sizes vary depending on the plant source, isolation procedure, and measurement method. They contain diverse biomolecules, including lipids, proteins, microRNAs, and phytochemicals, and have been investigated for their potential roles i
papers.summary: This review examines plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) as natural nanocarriers for delivering bioactive compounds, highlighting their lipid-bilayer structure and cargo of lipids, proteins, microRNAs, and phytochemicals. It discusses how PDEV size and composition vary by plant source and isolation method, and surveys their potential applications in functional foods and precision health technologies.

papers.title: The association of the gut microbiome with intermediate markers of breast cancer risk-mammographic density and blood steroid hormones-in the multiethnic cohort study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota may influence breast cancer risk through different biologic pathways. This analysis examined the association of the gut microbial composition with percent mammographic density (PMD), a strong predictor of breast cancer risk.
papers.summary: This study examines whether gut microbiome composition is associated with two intermediate markers of breast cancer risk—percent mammographic density and blood steroid hormone levels—in a multiethnic cohort. It tests the hypothesis that gut microbes influence breast cancer risk through hormonal and density-related pathways. The findings could clarify whether the microbiome is a viable target for risk stratification or prevention.

papers.title: Identification of Genes Associated with Gut Microbiota Metabolites in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Complicated by Acute Cerebral Infarction Based on Bioinformatics and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Background: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and acute cerebral infarction (ACI) are globally prevalent diseases that impose substantial public health burdens. While gut microbiota (GM) is increasingly recognized to regulate metabolic and immune homeostasis linked to both diseases, its shared genetically predicted microbial taxa and underlying metabolite-gene regulatory mechanisms in T2DM and ACI remain unclear, highlighting the need for systematic investigation. Accordingly, this study aimed to elucidate their regulatory mechanisms. Methods: Transcriptomic datasets, genome-wide association stu
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic data with Mendelian randomization to identify gut microbiota taxa and metabolites that may be causally linked to type 2 diabetes complicated by acute cerebral infarction, and to nominate genes mediating these metabolite effects. It provides a bioinformatics framework connecting microbiome-derived metabolites to shared genetic mechanisms across the two conditions.

papers.title: Exploratory Shotgun Metagenomic Analysis of the Fecal Microbiome and Antimicrobial-Resistance Potential in Simmental Calves with Different Diarrheal Statuses.
papers.abstract: Calf diarrhea is frequently accompanied by disruption of the gastrointestinal microbiota, but the relationships between clinical status and microbial community composition, gene-content functional potential, and antimicrobial-resistance-associated features remain incompletely characterized. This exploratory study aimed to characterize these features in calves with different diarrheal statuses using shotgun metagenomics. Six approximately 2-month-old Simmental calves from Chahar Right Middle Banner, Inner Mongolia, were included, comprising two healthy calves, two calves with mild diarrhea, and
papers.summary: This exploratory study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the fecal microbiome and antimicrobial-resistance gene content of six Simmental calves with different diarrheal statuses (healthy, mild diarrhea, and presumably severe diarrhea). The small sample size limits statistical power, but the work characterizes how microbial community composition and resistance potential may shift with clinical status. It provides preliminary descriptive data rather than definitive conclusions about microbiome-diarrhea relationships.

papers.title: Limited Gut Microbiome Differences Between Relapsing-Remitting and Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Shotgun Metagenomic Study.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome may contribute to multiple sclerosis (MS) pathophysiology, but its relationship with disease phenotype and progression remains unclear. To characterize taxonomic and functional gut microbiome differences between relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) and secondary progressive MS (SPMS) and their associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers. This cross-sectional study included 89 participants (30 healthy controls, 29 RRMS, and 30 SPMS). Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to assess microbial diversity, taxonomic profiles, and predefined short-chain fatty ac
papers.summary: This cross-sectional shotgun metagenomic study compared gut microbiome composition and function across 30 healthy controls, 29 relapsing-remitting MS patients, and 30 secondary progressive MS patients. The authors found only limited taxonomic and functional differences between RRMS and SPMS, suggesting that gut microbiome shifts do not strongly distinguish these disease phenotypes. Associations with disability and circulating biomarkers were modest, indicating the microbiome's role in MS progression may be subtler than previously hypothesized.

papers.title: From Microbiome Associations to Deployable Precision Probiotics in Animals: A Critical Narrative Review and Proposed Causal Evidence Framework for Next-Generation Probiotic Development.
papers.abstract: Next-generation probiotics (NGPs) are promoted as precision tools for animal health, yet the term is often applied to uncommon taxa before causality, safety and target-species efficacy are established. This critical narrative review reframes animal NGPs as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic category. A structured PubMed search was last run on 14 September 2026 with a publication date cutoff of 1 September 2026 and was supplemented by citation tracing and targeted searches of authoritative sources. From the screened literature, 45 representative and conceptually informative sources w
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This critical narrative review argues that "next-generation probiotics" for animals should be defined as a development pathway rather than a taxonomic label, since many candidate taxa are promoted before causality, safety, and target-species efficacy are established. The authors synthesize 45 representative sources and propose a causal evidence framework to guide the progression from microbiome associations to deployable precision probiotics.

papers.title: Rethinking Solid-Phase Microextraction (SPME) for Bioanalysis: Workflow Optimisation in Automated Vacuum-Assisted Cooling SPME for Fatty Acid Monitoring in Faecal Waters.
papers.abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are key biomarkers of gut microbiota and intestinal health, yet their analysis is challenging due to high volatility, hydrophilicity, and the complexity of the faecal matrix. This study introduces a novel, green, and fully automated workflow for monitoring SCFAs in faecal water samples. It combines microwave-assisted derivatisation, vacuum-assisted cooling multiple solid-phase microextraction (Vac-HS-cooling-MSPME), and fast gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). On-sample derivatisation with 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzyl bromide was optimised via design of
papers.summary: This study presents a fully automated, green analytical workflow for measuring short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in faecal water, combining microwave-assisted derivatisation with vacuum-assisted cooling multiple solid-phase microextraction (Vac-HS-cooling-MSPME) and fast GC-MS. The method addresses the volatility, hydrophilicity, and matrix complexity challenges of SCFA analysis, with derivatisation conditions optimised via design of experiments. It offers a practical approach for monitoring gut microbiota-related biomarkers in complex biological samples.

papers.title: Network Pharmacology of Natural Products from Computational Prediction to Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Natural products are important sources of bioactive compounds, but their complex chemical composition and multi-target effects make their mechanisms difficult to investigate using conventional approaches. Network pharmacology provides a systems-level framework for integrating chemical, biological, and disease-related information to investigate these complex interactions. This review describes the network pharmacology workflow, from active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation and target prediction to network construction and pathway enrichment, and the complementary roles of molecular docking a
papers.summary: This review outlines the network pharmacology workflow for studying natural products, covering active-compound screening, ADMET evaluation, target prediction, network construction, and pathway enrichment, along with the complementary roles of molecular docking and experimental validation. It serves as a practical guide for integrating computational predictions with experimental confirmation in natural product research.

papers.title: Dynamics of Gut Microbial Community and Function in Growing Male Raccoon Dogs.
papers.abstract: Background: Raccoon dogs have short breeding cycles and strong adaptability, and their fur is economically valuable. Although the gut microbiota, a key regulator of animal health, has been extensively studied in livestock, its composition and function in raccoon dogs remain poorly understood. Methods: In this study, the gut microbiota structure and functional profiles of ten raccoon dogs were analyzed during their growth period, including 2 (M2), 3 (M3), 4 (M4), 6 (M6), and 8 (M8) months after birth. Results: Our findings revealed that the richness and diversity of the gut microbiota in growin
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study tracked the gut microbiota of ten male raccoon dogs across five time points (2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 months after birth) to characterize how community composition and function change during growth. The authors report that microbial richness and diversity shift over the growth period, providing a first descriptive profile of gut microbiota dynamics in this species. The work is largely descriptive and species-specific, with limited immediate relevance beyond raccoon dog husbandry and fur-farming research.

papers.title: Integrated Metagenomic and Metatranscriptomic Analysis Reveals Microbiome Differences Between Bisexual and Parthenogenetic Populations of Haemaphysalis longicornis.
papers.abstract: The tick Haemaphysalis longicornis is an important vector of human and animal pathogens in East Asia that comprises both bisexual (Bis) and parthenogenetic (Par) populations. While previous studies have documented differences between these reproductive groups in genome ploidy, host transcription, and vector capacity, it remains unclear whether reproductive strategy is accompanied by systematic divergence in the tick-associated microbiome, including microbial community composition, transcriptional activities, and functional outputs. Here, we profiled laboratory-maintained Bis and Par population
papers.summary: This study compared the microbiome of bisexual and parthenogenetic populations of the tick Haemaphysalis longicornis using integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic sequencing. The authors found systematic differences in microbial community composition, transcriptional activity, and functional outputs between the two reproductive groups, suggesting that reproductive strategy is accompanied by microbiome divergence. These findings link tick reproductive biology to microbiome structure and function, with potential implications for vector capacity.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals gut segment-specific and age-associated microbial restructuring linked to host phenotypic maturation in Taihu geese.
papers.abstract: Taihu geese are valued for efficient utilization of fibrous feed resources and for desirable meat quality, yet how gut microbial organization varies across intestinal regions and physiological stages, and how these changes relate to host phenotype, remains unclear. We integrated 16S rRNA gene sequencing, ITS sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and host phenotyping to characterize intestinal microbial ecology in Taihu geese at 160 days of age (D160; physiological stability stage) and 450 days of age (D450; late-laying stage). Spatial profiling of the D160 group across the duodenum, jejunum, ileum
papers.summary: This study integrates 16S rRNA, ITS, and shotgun metagenomic sequencing with host phenotyping to map how gut microbial communities differ across intestinal segments and between two physiological stages (160 vs. 450 days) in Taihu geese. It identifies segment-specific and age-associated microbial restructuring that correlates with host phenotypic maturation, highlighting how gut ecology shifts with physiological stage in this breed.

papers.title: Traditional Food Use and Ethnomedicinal Contexts of Turnip (Brassica rapa L.): A Scoping Review of Composition, Food Processing, and Health-Related Evidence.
papers.abstract: Turnip (Brassica rapa L.) is widely cultivated for food and has documented ethnomedicinal uses. This scoping review mapped the international literature on turnip, with detailed synthesis focused on turnip materials associated with selected regional food and ethnomedicinal traditions in China. Searches covered seven bibliographic databases. The bibliographic map comprised 771 records, of which 397 were selected for detailed synthesis. Regional uses varied in plant part and preparation method. The clearest evidence concerned composition and processing: constituent profiles differed by provenance
papers.summary: This scoping review mapped 771 records on turnip (Brassica rapa), synthesizing 397 in detail, focusing on regional food and ethnomedicinal traditions, especially in China. The clearest evidence concerned composition and processing, with constituent profiles varying by provenance and preparation method, while health-related evidence was less well established. The review highlights gaps between traditional use claims and rigorous health-outcome data.

papers.title: Soil Microbiome Signatures Associated with Epidemiological Heterogeneity Across Natural Plague Foci in Inner Mongolia, China.
papers.abstract: Plague persistence relies on complex host-vector-environment interactions, yet the ecological contribution of soil microbiomes to natural foci remains poorly understood. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples across four distinct plague foci in Inner Mongolia, China, to characterize microbiome features associated with contrasting epidemiological states. Taxonomic, functional, and network analyses showed that the three active plague foci exhibited lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa, particularly Streptomyces. Co
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 143 soil samples from four plague foci in Inner Mongolia revealed that active plague foci had lower microbial diversity, simplified co-occurrence networks, and enrichment of specific taxa such as Streptomyces compared to inactive foci. These soil microbiome signatures correlate with epidemiological heterogeneity, suggesting the soil microbiome may play an ecological role in plague persistence.

papers.title: Fast and accurate taxonomic domain assignment of short metagenomic reads using BBERT.
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomes from complex environments such as soil uncover vast biodiversity. Yet most short reads produced by shotgun sequencing cannot be taxonomically or functionally annotated, as they lack a sufficiently comprehensive reference, obscuring the true structure and function of microbial communities. We introduce BBERT, a nucleotide large language model optimized for short reads. Testing on a large cohort of soil metagenomes, we found that BBERT identifies bacterial sequence syntax without relying on reference databases, enabling accurate assignment of taxonomic domain, coding potentia
papers.summary: BBERT is a nucleotide large language model trained to classify short metagenomic reads by taxonomic domain without relying on reference databases. Tested on soil metagenomes, it accurately assigns bacterial sequences and identifies coding potential, addressing the large fraction of reads that current reference-based methods leave unannotated.

papers.title: Dietary Fibre in Pea Cotyledon Used as a Protein Source Provides Multidimensional Protection Against Colonic Protein Putrefaction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Substitution of plant-based for animal-based protein sources has been recommended to reduce global non-communicable disease burdens, including colorectal cancer. Objective: The goal of this study was to determine possible ways that pea cotyledon may modulate hindgut concentrations of protein putrefaction products implicated in colorectal cancer by comparing diets based on casein, meat or pea cotyledon in a rat model. Method: Rats (n = 8 per treatment) were fed for 9 days on 18.6% protein diets containing casein, meat, or yellow split peas as sole protein sources. Faecal
papers.summary: In a rat feeding study, replacing casein or meat protein with pea cotyledon as the sole protein source reduced hindgut markers of protein putrefaction, compounds linked to colorectal cancer risk. The authors attribute this protective effect to the fibre content of peas acting alongside the plant protein. This suggests pea-based protein sources may offer multidimensional benefits for colon health compared with animal proteins.

papers.title: Short-Term Simulated NH4+/NO3- Inputs Reorganize Soil Microbial Communities and Modify N-Cycling Functional Potential in Temperate Forests.
papers.abstract: Forest soil nitrogen (N) turnover and nitrous oxide (N2O) release are strongly influenced by atmospheric N deposition. Although the effects of individual inorganic N species on soil biogeochemistry are well documented, the consequences of changing their relative supply for N2O formation and the underlying microbial pathways remain less clear. We therefore examined soil N2O emissions, microbial communities, and N-transformation potential across a gradient of ammonium-to-nitrate (NH4+/NO3-) inputs in a temperate forest soil from Northeast China. Seven treatments covering NH4+/NO3- ratios from 1:
papers.summary: This study tested how different ratios of ammonium to nitrate inputs affect soil microbial communities and nitrogen cycling in temperate forest soil from Northeast China. The authors found that shifting the NH4+/NO3- balance reorganizes microbial community composition and alters the functional potential for nitrogen transformations, with implications for nitrous oxide emissions. The work highlights that the relative supply of inorganic N species, not just total N load, shapes soil biogeochemistry.

papers.title: Intratumoral Bacterial Profiles, Bacterial Co-Detection Patterns, and Molecular Alterations in Colorectal Cancer and Colorectal Polyps: A Vietnamese Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Intratumoral microbiota may contribute to colorectal cancer (CRC), but their relationships with bacterial co-occurrence, relative bacterial loads, and molecular alterations remain incompletely understood. This study characterized intratumoral bacterial profiles in CRC and colorectal polyps and examined their clinicopathological and molecular associations. A cross-sectional study included 149 patients with CRC and 109 patients with benign colorectal polyps. F. nucleatum, ETBF, A. muciniphila, and eae+E. coli were detected in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues using multiplex real-time PC
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study profiled intratumoral bacteria (F. nucleatum, ETBF, A. muciniphila, and eae+ E. coli) in FFPE tissues from 149 Vietnamese colorectal cancer patients and 109 patients with benign polyps using multiplex real-time PCR. It examined how bacterial detection patterns relate to clinicopathological features and molecular alterations, aiming to clarify bacterial co-occurrence and load patterns in colorectal tumorigenesis.

papers.title: Synovial SLC1A5-Associated Amino Acid Metabolic Features in Knee Osteoarthritis: An Integrated Analysis of Synovial Transcriptomics, Fecal Metabolomics, and Gut Microbiota.
papers.abstract: Background: This exploratory study aimed to characterize amino acid related features in osteoarthritis (OA). Methods: We analyzed independent public synovial transcriptomic datasets and paired fecal metabolomics and 16S ribosomal RNA profiles from 20 patients with knee OA and 14 controls. Metabolite-sensing genes were intersected with nominally differential genes and prioritized using elastic net, support vector machine recursive feature elimination, and extreme gradient boosting. Results:SLC1A5 (solute carrier family 1 member 5) expression was lower in the discovery cohort GSE89408 (log2 fold
papers.summary: This exploratory study integrated public synovial transcriptomic data with paired fecal metabolomics and 16S rRNA profiles from knee osteoarthritis patients and controls to identify amino acid metabolic features. SLC1A5, a solute carrier gene, showed reduced expression in OA synovium and was prioritized by multiple machine learning methods, suggesting a link between synovial amino acid metabolism and gut microbiome-derived metabolites in OA.

papers.title: Bifidobacterium longum Depletion and Bile Acid Dysregulation in MASLD: Links to Hepatic TGR5-AMPK Signaling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease worldwide. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis and aberrant bile acid metabolism are central to MASLD pathogenesis, the critical keystone species and precise molecular mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we performed an integrated analysis of 14 public 16S rRNA datasets (275 controls, 352 patients), combining multi-method differential abundance screening, machine learning, and network analysis to pinpoint MASLD-specific microbial signatures. We further validated the therapeutic potential of can
papers.summary: This study integrated 14 public 16S rRNA datasets to identify Bifidobacterium longum as a key species depleted in MASLD, alongside bile acid dysregulation. The authors link these microbial and metabolic changes to hepatic TGR5-AMPK signaling, suggesting a mechanistic pathway and potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Microbiome-Related Amino-Acid Profiles of Liver and Muscle Tissues in Arbor Acres Broiler Chickens.
papers.abstract: The study, designed as a group-level integrative data analysis, included homogeneous datasets obtained from 24 Arbor Acres chicken groups. Quantitative amino-acid analysis in chicken tissues was carried out using the capillary electrophoresis method. Gut microbial community analysis was performed using 16S rRNA gene-sequencing technology on the Illumina MiSeq platform. Amino-acid analysis of liver samples revealed 10 Arg-high and 14 Arg-low chicken groups, while for thigh samples, the ratio of Arg-high and Arg-low groups was 18/6, respectively. The gut microbiomes of chickens with an Arg-high
papers.summary: This study profiled amino acids in liver and thigh muscle tissue from 24 groups of Arbor Acres broiler chickens and correlated them with gut microbiome composition using 16S rRNA sequencing. Groups were classified as having high or low arginine levels in liver (10 high, 14 low) and thigh (18 high, 6 low), and the microbiomes of arginine-high chickens were compared. The work suggests links between gut microbial communities and tissue amino-acid profiles in poultry.

papers.title: Next-Generation Sequencing in Practical Wildlife Disease Investigation: Metagenomic Insights into European Bison and Gazelle Mortality and Morbidity Events.
papers.abstract: Wildlife disease investigations require diagnostic methods capable of detecting diverse and previously unrecognized pathogens. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) was applied to samples from three Dorcas gazelles (Gazella dorcas osiris) affected by sudden mortality and four European bison (Bison bonasus) with respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis (NBP). No dominant bacterial species was detected in gazelles. In European bison, respiratory disease was associated with Pasteurella multocida, whereas NBP samples were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. Dorcas
papers.summary: This study applied metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to investigate mortality and morbidity events in captive wildlife, analyzing samples from three Dorcas gazelles with sudden death and four European bison with respiratory disease or necrotic balanoposthitis. No dominant bacterial pathogen was identified in the gazelles, while respiratory disease in bison was associated with Pasteurella multocida and the genital lesions were dominated by Porphyromonas levii and other anaerobes. The work demonstrates that mNGS can provide actionable pathogen insights in wildlife disease investigations where conventional diagnostics fall short.

papers.title: Sketching the SRA: experiment-wide similarity search across 4.8 million metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Recent efforts have demonstrated that systematic analysis of the millions of metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) enables groundbreaking biological discoveries. However, SRA-scale comparison of whole metagenomes has remained elusive. Here, we introduce the most comprehensive resource to date for experiment-to-experiment analysis of all SRA metagenomes, comprising FracMinHash sketches (470GB), hypergen sketches (19GB), and an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix (90GB), which we release online at https://github.com/RolandFaure/SRA-metagenome-sketches-databases . These resources enable
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors created a comprehensive resource for comparing all 4.8 million metagenomes in the Sequence Read Archive using compact FracMinHash and hypergen sketches, along with an all-pairs Jaccard similarity matrix. This enables experiment-wide similarity search across the entire SRA metagenome collection for the first time, opening the door to large-scale discovery from public data.

papers.title: Maternal transmission and limited virulent phage replication shape early infant gut virome maturation.
papers.abstract: Early life gut microbiome dynamics are increasingly recognized as important determinants of microbiome maturation, yet the ecological dynamics of its associated bacteriophages remain poorly resolved. Here, we performed bulk and virus like particle (VLP)-enriched metagenomic sequencing and fecal metabolomic profiling of longitudinal fecal samples from 32 mother-infant dyads, incorporating an exogenous phage spike in to enable absolute quantification of viral loads. Our results show that early infant gut phageome is defined by a profound lack of virulent phage genome copies while temperate phage
papers.summary: This study used longitudinal metagenomic and metabolomic profiling of 32 mother-infant pairs, with an exogenous phage spike-in for absolute viral load quantification, to track early gut virome development. It found that the early infant gut phageome is characterized by very low absolute abundance of virulent phage genomes, with temperate phages dominating, and that maternal transmission shapes the infant virome. These findings suggest that virulent phage replication is limited in early life, which may have implications for how the infant gut microbiome matures.

papers.title: Comparative Genomics of Ecologically Differentiated Nitrososphaera-Related Ammonia-Oxidizing Archaea.
papers.abstract: Soil acidification strongly influences the ecology of terrestrial ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA). Within this group, the Nitrososphaera-related alpha (NS-α) and delta (NS-δ) lineages exhibit pronounced pH-associated ecological differentiation. In the preceding microcosm experiment, NS-α populations showed greater persistence than NS-δ during ammonium-driven soil acidification, yet the genomic basis underlying this ecological differentiation remains poorly understood. In this study, metagenomic sequencing of one near-neutral baseline microcosm (pH 7.35) and one acidified microcosm (pH 4.73) wa
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing of soil microcosms at near-neutral (pH 7.35) and acidified (pH 4.73) conditions to compare the genomes of two ecologically differentiated ammonia-oxidizing archaeal lineages, NS-α and NS-δ. The work links genomic differences between these Nitrososphaera-related lineages to their previously observed differences in persistence under ammonium-driven soil acidification, providing a genomic basis for pH-associated ecological differentiation.

papers.title: Complementary Use of Shotgun Metagenomics and Multiplex PCR for Pathogen Detection on High-Touch Surfaces.
papers.abstract: Shotgun metagenomics is being increasingly promoted as a pathogen-agnostic alternative to targeted PCR for environmental surveillance, yet its practical value on dry, low-biomass, host-dominated surfaces remains uncertain. In a companion study, we reported QIAstat-Dx multiplex PCR screening of 55 pooled high-touch surface samples from Riyadh, identifying 19 positive pools (34.5%). Here, in a retrospective exploratory comparison, we use those previously reported PCR calls as the targeted comparator and ask what unenriched shotgun metagenomic sequencing adds. Ten archived pools, each with at lea
papers.summary: This study compared shotgun metagenomic sequencing with multiplex PCR for detecting pathogens on high-touch environmental surfaces in Riyadh. Using 10 archived PCR-positive pools, the authors found that unenriched shotgun metagenomics adds limited pathogen detection value on dry, low-biomass, host-dominated surfaces, suggesting PCR remains the more practical targeted approach while metagenomics may offer complementary, pathogen-agnostic context.

papers.title: Immunomodulatory and Metabolic Effects of Ginsenosides Rg1/Rb1 in IBD, RA, and MASLD: Targeting Gut Microbiota-Autoimmunity Axis.
papers.abstract: Panax ginseng Meyer has been commonly used as a traditional herbal medicine in East Asia for millennia. Ginsenosides Rg1 and Rb1 are the primary pharmacologically active ingredients and exhibit broad therapeutic efficacy against immunometabolic disorders, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). To summarize the protective roles of these ginsenosides and investigate their underlying mechanisms, we integrated literature evidence with network pharmacology and gut microbiota-host gene association a
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that ginsenosides Rg1 and Rb1 from Panax ginseng alleviate inflammatory bowel disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and rheumatoid arthritis by modulating gut microbiota and host immune-metabolic pathways. Using network pharmacology and microbiota-host gene association analyses, the authors map shared mechanisms linking these compounds to the gut microbiota-autoimmunity axis. The work positions ginsenosides as multi-target therapeutic candidates for immunometabolic disorders.

papers.title: Taxonomic and Functional Profiles of the Gastrointestinal Microbiome Across Digestive Tract Segments in Growing Water Buffaloes.
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal segments in ruminants differ in physiological environment and substrate availability. This study characterized taxonomic and gene-encoded functional profiles in 54 shotgun metagenomes from 30 growing male water buffaloes assigned to five dietary formulations. The dataset comprised 30 rumen-fluid samples, six per group, and 24 post-slaughter samples from six gastrointestinal sites in five animals. Comparisons among groups A-E yielded p = 0.9816 for final body weight, p = 0.9315 for overall average daily gain, and p = 0.2832 for rumen-fluid pH. Genus-level principal coordinate a
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to profile the taxonomic and functional composition of the gastrointestinal microbiome across multiple digestive tract segments in growing water buffaloes fed five different diets. The authors found that diet formulation did not significantly affect body weight, average daily gain, or rumen pH, and they characterized how microbial communities and gene-encoded functions vary by gut segment. The dataset provides a reference for understanding segment-specific microbiome structure in a ruminant livestock species.

papers.title: First Shotgun Metagenomic Characterization of the Gut Microbiome of the Endangered Longhorn Beetle Callipogon relictus (Coleoptera: Cerambycidae).
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome of Callipogon relictus, a rare member of the family Cerambycidae, was characterized for the first time using shotgun metagenomic sequencing. The aim of this study was to compare the taxonomic diversity and structure of the gut microbial communities in larvae and adults. Bacteria dominated the metagenomic profiles, accounting for 92.47% of the taxonomic composition in adults and 85.31% in larvae. Proteobacteria predominated in the bacterial component of both pooled profiles, accounting for 87.88% and 89.43%, respectively. The pooled adult profile had the highest relative abun
papers.summary: This study provides the first shotgun metagenomic characterization of the gut microbiome of the endangered longhorn beetle Callipogon relictus, comparing larval and adult life stages. Bacteria dominated the communities (85–92%), with Proteobacteria being the most abundant phylum in both stages. The work establishes a baseline description of gut microbial diversity in this rare species.

papers.title: Differential Regulation of Postoperative Gut Microbiota by Inhalation vs Intravenous Anesthesia: NF-κB/HIF-1α-Mediated Macrophage Polarization.
papers.abstract: Perioperative anesthetic strategies are increasingly recognized as important modulators of postoperative immune responses and intestinal microecological homeostasis following gastrointestinal surgery.
papers.summary: This study compares how two common anesthesia approaches—inhaled versus intravenous—affect the gut microbiome and immune response after gastrointestinal surgery. The authors propose that the inhaled anesthetic alters macrophage polarization through NF-κB/HIF-1α signaling, leading to distinct postoperative shifts in gut bacterial composition compared with intravenous anesthesia.

papers.title: Human milk oligosaccharides are distinctly processed by early life gut microbial sialidases.
papers.abstract: The infant gut microbiome in early life is shaped by numerous factors, including feeding method. Exclusively breastfed and formula-fed infants exhibit distinct microbiome compositions. While these effects are well-established, the underlying mechanisms that drive these differences are not fully understood. Here, we examine the removal of sialic acid from human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) influenced by human microbial sialidases in early life. We identify 351 and 214 unique sialidase sequences from adult and infant microbiome metagenomes, respectively, and characterize a diverse, representativ
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes sialidase enzymes from early-life gut microbiomes that remove sialic acid from human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs). By mining metagenomes, the authors found 351 sialidase sequences in adults and 214 in infants, revealing that infant gut microbes process HMOs in distinct ways. These findings help explain mechanistic differences between breastfed and formula-fed infant microbiome compositions.

papers.title: WasteFams: a database of protein families from global wastewater microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Wastewater surveillance has emerged as a critical tool for global epidemiology, yet the functional diversity of wastewater microbiomes remains poorly characterized at the protein level. Here, we present WasteFams, the first comprehensive database dedicated to the systematic exploration of protein families in wastewater metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies worldwide. Integrating data from 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (504 metagenomes, 129 metatranscriptomes, and 1151 reference genomes after filtering), WasteFams catalogs 3887 non-redundant protein fa
papers.summary: WasteFams is a new database that catalogs protein families found in wastewater microbiomes worldwide, built from 580 metagenomes, 132 metatranscriptomes, and 1709 reference genomes (filtered to 504, 129, and 1151 respectively). It provides the first systematic, protein-level characterization of functional diversity in wastewater microbial communities, supporting both wastewater surveillance and broader microbiome research.

papers.title: Phenotypic and genomic characterization of a halophilic sulfate-reducing bacterium Desulfoplanes aerotolerans sp. nov. from a petroleum reservoir and its possible implication in pipeline corrosion.
papers.abstract: The issue of biogenic corrosion of steel equipment is especially pressing for petroleum reservoirs with high-salinity formation water containing sulfate. The predominance of sulfate-reducing bacteria of the genus Desulfoplanes in formation water samples from petroleum reservoirs in Tatarstan (Russia) was previously demonstrated using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomic analysis. The present study is devoted to the isolation, phenotypic and genomic characterization of the sulfate-reducing bacterial strain Desulfoplanes sp. PS50T and its involvement in steel corrosion. Studying the
papers.summary: The authors isolated and characterized a new halophilic sulfate-reducing bacterium, Desulfoplanes aerotolerans sp. nov. strain PS50T, from a petroleum reservoir in Tatarstan. Phenotypic and genomic analyses describe its salt tolerance, oxygen tolerance, and sulfate-reducing metabolism, and link the strain to steel corrosion relevant to oilfield pipelines. The work provides a cultured representative of a genus previously detected only through 16S rRNA and metagenomic surveys.

papers.title: Gut microbiome taxonomic and functional capacity alterations in CHD and HFpEF.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is known to modulate metabolic health, yet its role in coronary heart disease (CHD) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains unclear. In the present study, we profiled the gut microbiome of 234 participants using shotgun metagenomic sequencing across controls (n = 43), individuals with low-risk atherosclerosis (LRAS, n = 23), and patients with CHD + HFpEF (n = 168). Species richness was significantly increased in CHD + HFpEF, with no disruption in taxonomic evenness. LRAS did not diverge significantly in alpha metrics. In contrast, beta diversity an
papers.summary: Shotgun metagenomic profiling of 234 participants found that patients with combined coronary heart disease and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (CHD+HFpEF) had significantly higher gut microbiome species richness than controls, without loss of taxonomic evenness, while low-risk atherosclerosis showed no alpha-diversity divergence. Beta diversity and functional capacity analyses further distinguished the disease group, suggesting disease-associated shifts in microbiome composition and metabolic potential.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing for culture-negative anaerobic central nervous system infection involving Prevotella oris: attribution challenges in low-biomass specimens.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic central nervous system (CNS) infections are uncommon but diagnostically difficult because fastidious organisms may be suppressed by empirical antimicrobial therapy and conventional cultures may remain negative. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can recover microbial nucleic acids in this setting, but low microbial biomass creates a central attribution problem: a detected organism may represent active infection, introduced commensal DNA, laboratory background, or bioinformatic misclassification. This narrative Mini Review uses Prevotella oris as a
papers.summary: This mini-review examines the diagnostic challenges of using cerebrospinal fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to identify anaerobic CNS infections, using Prevotella oris as a case example. The authors highlight that low microbial biomass in CSF makes it difficult to determine whether a detected organism represents true infection versus contamination, commensal DNA, or misclassification. The review discusses attribution challenges and likely offers guidance for interpreting mNGS results in culture-negative anaerobic CNS infections.

papers.title: gTranslate: rapid and accurate translation table prediction for prokaryotic genomes.
papers.abstract: Bioinformatic tools often require the prediction of protein-coding genes to make inferences about prokaryotic genomes. Typically, the genetic code used for translating genes to proteins must be specified by the user based on the taxonomic classification of a genome assembly or, for some widely used tools, established using a heuristic rule based on gene coding densities. Manual specification is at best inconvenient, but more challenging is that many bioinformatic tools are applied before taxonomic classifications have been established making specifying the translation table impractical.
papers.summary: gTranslate is a new tool that predicts the correct genetic code (translation table) for prokaryotic genomes without requiring prior taxonomic classification. It addresses a common bottleneck in genome annotation pipelines where the translation table must be manually specified or guessed heuristically, enabling more automated and accurate protein-coding gene prediction.

papers.title: Metagenomic and metabolomic analysis of the early gut microbiota development in Nipponia nippon.
papers.abstract: The crested ibis (Nipponia nippon) is an endangered bird whose early gut microbiota development remains poorly understood. To address this gap, this study integrated metagenomics and metabolomics to investigate the dynamic succession of gut microbiota and metabolism in naturally hatched chicks during early development.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics and metabolomics to track how the gut microbiota and metabolic profiles of endangered crested ibis chicks change during early development. It provides one of the first integrated characterizations of microbial succession in this species, which may inform conservation and captive-rearing strategies.

papers.title: Metagenomic and culture-dependent characterization of between-field variation in phosphorus-cycling microbial communities and functional potential across tobacco-safflower rotation fields.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms contribute to soil phosphorus (P) transformation and plant P acquisition, but P-cycling microbial communities and functional associations across tobacco-safflower rotation fields remain poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study combines metagenomic sequencing and culture-based methods to characterize phosphorus-cycling microbial communities in the rhizosphere across tobacco-safflower rotation fields, examining how these communities and their functional potential vary between fields. The work provides a baseline characterization of P-cycling taxa and genes in this rotation system, highlighting between-field variation that may influence soil phosphorus transformation and plant P acquisition.

papers.title: Pathway-level analysis suggests a maintenance-oriented transcriptional response of the ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosospira sp. NT to acidic pH.
papers.abstract: Acidic environments impose energetic constraints on ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), although some acid-tolerant lineages remain capable of ammonia oxidation at low pH. The transcriptional responses of acid-tolerant AOB to low-pH conditions remain poorly resolved. Here, we characterized the pathway-level response of Nitrosospira sp. NT by integrating a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome with comparative metatranscriptomic data from cultures incubated for 24 h at pH 5.0 or pH 8.0. Transcript abundance was not uniformly reduced among the metabolic pathways examined at pH 5.0. Genes assoc
papers.summary: The study examines how the acid-tolerant ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosospira sp. NT responds transcriptionally to low pH (5.0 vs. 8.0) over 24 hours, using a reconstructed metagenome-assembled genome and comparative metatranscriptomics. Rather than a uniform shutdown of metabolism, the pathway-level analysis suggests a maintenance-oriented response at acidic pH, with transcript abundance not uniformly reduced across metabolic pathways. This provides insight into how acid-tolerant AOB cope with energetic constraints in acidic environments.

papers.title: Bacterial metagenome in plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without OSCC by next-generation sequencing.
papers.abstract: Oral dysbiosis has been associated with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC); however, most microbiome studies rely on 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing, limiting species-level taxonomic resolution.
papers.summary: This study uses next-generation metagenomic sequencing to profile bacterial communities in plaque, saliva, and tumor samples from individuals with and without oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), moving beyond the species-level limitations of 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The work provides a higher-resolution characterization of oral dysbiosis associated with OSCC across multiple sample types.

papers.title: Baseline co-occurrence of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii is associated with greater increases in selected short-chain fatty acid-related pathways following resistant starch type 2 intervention across diverse populations.
papers.abstract: Type 2 resistant starch (RS2) can be fermented by the gut microbiota and contribute to short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production; however, microbial responses to resistant starch vary substantially across individuals and populations, and the role of baseline microbiota in this variability remains incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated four publicly available paired metagenomic datasets representing diverse experimental and host contexts and performed cross-dataset analyses of taxonomic and functional responses. Faecalibacterium prausnitzii was among the taxa consistently enriched
papers.summary: This study integrated four public metagenomic datasets to show that individuals whose baseline gut microbiota already contains both Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Ruminococcus bromii tend to have larger increases in short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-related microbial pathways after eating type 2 resistant starch. The finding suggests baseline microbial co-occurrence patterns help explain why people respond differently to the same dietary fiber.

papers.title: Gut microbiome and gut-derived metabolites to identify the transition from metabolically healthy to unhealthy obesity: a mini review.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a metabolically heterogeneous condition with distinct metabolic phenotypes, ranging from metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) to metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). Although individuals with MHO initially lack cardiometabolic dysfunction, many transition to MUO over time, exponentially increasing their risk for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. In this mini-review, we synthesize recent evidence from multi-omic cohort studies evaluating gut microbiome composition and gut-derived metabolites as functional biomarkers of obesity heterogeneity and drivers of metabolic decline
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes evidence that gut microbiome composition and gut-derived metabolites can serve as functional biomarkers distinguishing metabolically healthy obesity (MHO) from metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO), and may help predict the transition between these states. The authors argue that multi-omic cohort data support a role for microbial and metabolite signatures as drivers of metabolic decline, potentially enabling earlier risk stratification for type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Investigating the Effect of Oral Probiotic Capsules on Postpartum Sleep Quality in Primiparous Women: A triple-blind randomised controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Quality of sleep is an important indicator of health. Sleep disturbance and daytime fatigue is one of the most common problems in the postpartum period. Early postpartum (first 4 weeks) is when sleep is most disturbed. The gut microbiota may affect sleep quality and affect host health through the production of metabolites and compounds. This study aimed to determine the effect of oral probiotic capsule on the quality of sleep after delivery in primiparous women.
papers.summary: This triple-blind randomised controlled trial tested whether oral probiotic capsules improve sleep quality in first-time mothers during the early postpartum period, a window when sleep disturbance is most severe. The study draws on the gut microbiota–sleep axis hypothesis, in which microbial metabolites may influence host sleep. It evaluates a low-cost, non-pharmacological intervention for a common postpartum health problem.

papers.title: Evaluating traditional Chinese medicine modulation of the gut microbiota-bile acid axis in metabolic and inflammatory diseases: mechanistic evidence and translational priorities.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D), and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are clinically distinct disorders that share perturbations in intestinal ecology, bile-acid composition, epithelial barrier function, and immune-metabolic regulation. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) may modify these interconnected processes, but the translational significance of reported effects remains uncertain. Changes in microbial composition are often interpreted as mechanisms without evidence of altered microbial function, bile-acid profiles o
papers.summary: This review examines how traditional Chinese medicine may influence metabolic and inflammatory diseases (MASLD, obesity, T2D, IBD) through the gut microbiota–bile acid axis. The authors argue that many reported microbial shifts are over-interpreted as mechanisms without functional or bile-acid evidence, and they outline translational priorities to strengthen causal claims.

papers.title: Metabolomics in the wild: A scoping review of non-invasive methods for understanding vertebrate wildlife health and success.
papers.abstract: An increase in metabolomics research over the last decade has expanded species-specific knowledge of biological processes, but has primarily focused upon humans, domesticated and model animal species. Recent advances, particularly around data management pipelines for untargeted studies, make the field more accessible to disciplines outside those embedded in analytical chemistry, including wildlife conservation. To establish the breadth of existing wild vertebrate animal metabolomic research, specifically utilising non-invasive sampling, this scoping review establishes: (1) general trends in pu
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the use of non-invasive metabolomics sampling methods in wild vertebrate research, finding that the field is still in its early stages and has primarily focused on humans, domesticated, and model species rather than wildlife. The authors highlight that recent advances in untargeted data management pipelines make metabolomics more accessible to conservation scientists, and they identify general trends and gaps in applying these methods to understand wildlife health and success.

papers.title: Probiotics in type 1 diabetes: immunomodulatory mechanisms and the unresolved question of clinical efficacy.
papers.abstract: Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) is a common autoimmune disease worldwide, which is associated with imbalanced gut microbiota. Intestinal dysbiosis plays a key role in the pathogenesis of T1D, and it may affect immune tolerance and autoimmune responses of pancreatic islet β-cells. As a potential immunomodulator, probiotics can help restore this balance, regulate immune responses, and reduce the risk of T1D. Although probiotics offer a logical immunomodulatory strategy to restore microbial and immune homeostasis, the translational gap between robust preclinical mechanisms and inconsistent clinical outcome
papers.summary: This review examines how gut microbiome imbalance contributes to type 1 diabetes pathogenesis and evaluates probiotics as a potential immunomodulatory strategy to restore microbial and immune homeostasis. The authors highlight that while preclinical mechanistic evidence is robust, clinical trial results remain inconsistent, leaving the translational efficacy of probiotics in T1D unresolved.
